result.reason: The New York governing-law language is acceptable, but the venue provisions are internally inconsistent. The clause gives New York County courts exclusive jurisdiction over any dispute while requiring the same disputes to be resolved by binding arbitration, and it still permits award confirmation in any court of competent jurisdiction, including where the losing party resides. Adding a New York arbitration seat also goes beyond the stated court-venue playbook and changes the existing arbitration arrangement. The dispute-resolution provisions should distinguish arbitration from court proceedings and make New York County courts exclusive for arbitration-related relief and enforcement if arbitration is to remain.
